commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: artifact-diagramming
commands.description: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.

commands.name: artifact-capabilities
commands.description: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

Done. `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` reports **zero errors** for `server/router-groups/geometry-admin-router.ts`, and **no new error appears in any other file** (verified by diffing the full compiler output against a clean-tree baseline: 1068 → 1039 lines, and every one of the 29 eliminated lines belongs to the target file).

## What I fixed

The 13 TS18047 errors were the stated target, but the acceptance bar is zero errors in the file, and it had 24. All are fixed without suppressions.

**The 13 `'db' is possibly 'null'` errors** — `getDb()` returns `null` when `DATABASE_URL` is unset. Added a `requireDb()` helper that narrows the type by failing the request, and used it at the 7 call sites:

```ts
async function requireDb() {
  const db = await getDb();
  if (!db) {
    throw new TRPCError({ code: 'INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR', message: 'Database unavailable: …' });
  }
  return db;
}
```

I used `TRPCError` (already imported, and the file's idiom) rather than returning empty results, so an absent database can't render as zeros that look like real measurements on an admin dashboard.

**The other 11 errors:**
- `createLogger('geometry-admin-router')` — added the domain to the `LogDomain` union in `server/_core/logger.ts`. Verified `LogDomain` is only used as a parameter type (no exhaustive map over it), so this is purely additive. I preferred it over re-labelling the module's logs under an existing domain, and over the `as LogDomain` cast used elsewhere in the repo.
- `z.record(z.number())` — zod v4 requires `z.record(keyType, valueType)`. The single-arg form was being read as `Record<number, unknown>`, which alone accounted for four errors. Now `z.record(z.string(), z.number())`.
- `recordPreHook(...)` — was passing 3 of 5 required arguments; added `shouldConstrain` and `constraintsInjected.length`.
- The advanced neurocosmology hooks take a `CanonicalEmotionalState`, not the flat metric record. I project the diagnostic state onto the canonical base dimensions via the existing `createInitialState` / `updateBaseDimensions` factories and let the state module derive the rest.

## Two real bugs surfaced

Fixing these types rather than silencing them exposed live defects, both previously hidden behind `as any` (which my change removes — the file now contains no `any`, `ts-ignore`, or equivalent):

1. **`recordPostHook(loopDetected, computeTimeMs)` had its arguments swapped** — the signature is `(computeTimeMs, loopDetected)`. Post-hook latency was being recorded from a boolean.

2. **`fireTestAlert` could only ever fire 2 of its 7 alert types.** `evaluateAlerts` reads `loopDetected` from `postResult` and the singularity/phase-shift/invariant counts from `neuroAdvanced`, but all four were being set on `preResult`, where nothing reads them. Separately, `syntheticPre` had no `computeTimeMs`, so the degradation check summed to `NaN` and never tripped. Only `high_fixation_risk` and `high_drift_score` worked. I rebuilt the call as a properly typed `AlertEvaluationParams` with each value on the member the evaluator actually inspects, and checked the synthetic timings against the real threshold (200ms): 1000ms when degraded, 15ms otherwise.

Worth noting these are behavioral changes beyond a pure type fix — but they're the fix, since making the types honest is what revealed that the code didn't do what it claimed. The compiler-only outcome is unaffected either way.

Changes are confined to the repo, uncommitted and unpushed; `server/_core/logger.ts` is the only file touched besides the target.
